articles.title_orig: Hurricane Nolo expected to bring heavy rain as it skirts Hawaii’s Big Island
articles.title_zh: Hurricane Nolo expected to bring heavy rain as it skirts Hawaii’s Big Island
articles.content_orig:
NAALEHU, Hawaii — Hurricane Nolo is forecast to strengthen into a major hurricane in the Pacific Ocean over the weekend, unleashing intense rain, the possibility of life-threatening flash flooding, and dangerous surf for Hawaii’s Big Island.
Nolo was a Category 5 hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 160 mph early Saturday, the National Hurricane Center said, as its outer rainbands hit Big Island. Hurricane conditions are possible on the island, especially in areas with steep terrain, the weather service warned.
The storm was moving north-northwest at 10 mph on Saturday morning, but was expected to turn northeast and head toward Baja California Sur on Monday.
This marks the third hurricane in less than two months to whip past Hawaii (following Lala and Lowell ). The active Pacific hurricane season is likely due to a record-setting El Niño — a natural climate pattern characterized by a rise in sea surface temperatures in the eastern Pacific, and spawns more intense and frequent cyclones there.
Tess Kala, a South Point resident who grew up in the area, said the back-to-back storms are a shock to locals.
“Honestly, this is the first like, whoa, what happened? We had a lot of family and friends that have lived here all their lives through generations and never experienced this before,” she said.
Hawaii Gov. Josh Green said Friday that President Donald Trump approved the state’s request for an emergency declaration for Nolo to provide federal assistance for emergency protective measures across the state.
Mark Peters, a resident of Naalehu in the southern Big Island for seven years, said that the damage from the recent hurricanes has not been forgotten.
“It hurts me when I see friends and neighbors and people of this community that I know, and I just see it in their eyes, I hear it in their voices. We’ve been through a lot down here, and we still got a lot to go,” Peters said.
“We’re just getting started with our recovery. But to have yet another big storm hit us, and potentially even bigger than the last one, it’s difficult,” he said.
While he praised his community for its resilience, he said the people are still in need of basics like food and water, and many are in the process of reconstruction.
“We’re talking years. This is going to be a long recovery,” Peters said Friday.
He recalled driving through Waiohinu in the aftermath of Hurricane Lala and his “eyes getting wide open with all the damage, and the cars and houses moved and not where they’re supposed to be, and Waiohinu Park having buildings in the baseball field.”
Kala, the South Point resident, is preparing for Nolo by “moving everything away from the houses, tying things down, making sure that everything is hosed up and taped up as best as we possibly can.”
Nolo will bring periods of heavy rain that will continue across Big Island and Maui over the weekend, and could trigger life-threatening catastrophic flooding and mudslides, especially in steep terrain across eastern and southern portions of both Big Island and Maui, the hurricane center said.
Nolo is forecast to dump 8 to 12 inches of rain in eastern and southern parts of Big Island, with maximum amounts up to 16 inches. Western portions of Big Island could see one to three inches of rain with maximum amounts of six inches. Meanwhile, Maui could see four to six inches, with maximum amounts of eight inches, the National Hurricane Center said.
The rest of Hawaii will experience lesser rainfall totals but isolated flooding is possible.
Nolo could also bring large and damaging waves along portions of Big Island’s coastline into the weekend.
A hurricane watch and tropical storm warning are in effect for Hawaii County and a tropical storm watch is in effect for Maui County. A hurricane watch means that hurricane conditions are possible within 24-36 hours. A wind advisory has been issued for the rest of the state.
Tropical storm force winds will reach the Big Island on Friday afternoon, with hurricane force winds possible by late evening.
A high surf advisory is in effect for south and east facing shores of Big Island and east facing shores of Maui and Molokai. A high surf advisory was also issued for east facing shores of Niihau, Kauai, and Oahu beginning Friday evening.
Nolo could also spawn tornadoes and large waterspouts over and near Big Island and to the right of the track of the tropical cyclone.
Marlene Lenthang reported from Los Angeles and Ryan Chandler and Shanshan Dong from Naalehu.
Marlene Lenthang is a breaking news reporter for NBC News Digital.
Ryan Chandler is a correspondent for NBC News.

George Russell held off Max Verstappen for his first win in three months to cut into Kimi Antonelli’s standings lead at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
Russell started on pole and built a big lead before having to defend on two safety car restarts, before holding off Verstappen, who charged through the field from eighth to second and nearly chased down the Briton on the final lap.
Verstappen remains winless this year for the first time since his rookie season in 2016. Verstappen’s Red Bull teammate Isack Hadjar was third on his return from injury.
Antonelli started 16th after a crash in qualifying but ended up fifth as he limited the damage to his title lead, swerving to avoid a three-car crash ahead of him and later overtaking Lewis Hamilton.
It’s the Bahrain Grand Prix... in Malaysia. Here are the session times for that.

Saturday, October 3 FP3 – 5.30am Qualifying – 9am
Sunday, October 4 Race – 8am
A decent weekend for Haas, Red Bull and Lindblad. Williams should be happy with a point.
Too much for Russell to do but this performance should do wonders for his confidence. In fairness, he has driven well since the summer break.
“Win every race. My team-mate has had an incredible season, he’s been pretty flawless and now we’re getting to crunch time. I am going to focus on myself. It’s been a real tough period for me and I feel like I have come through the other side.”
“I am happy, it’s been very long six weeks. It’s been six weeks since I injured myself... this weekend I really too it step-by-step. It’s a track you can end up in the wall really quickly. It was a very slow build-up but it brought me here. I am very delighted.”
“We had a good race. The first stint was probably a bit difficult with the medium tyre but we worked out way into P3 and then we had a good restart... the yellow flag George lost a bit of boost in one corner. To the line I got close, but it was not enough.”
“It was amazing to be back on the top step of the podium. I want to say a big thank-you to my team. The first half of the race felt pretty plain sailing. All, in all incredible weekend. It’s just having more experience with this new driving style I’ve adopted. Every race since the break I feel like I’ve gone from strength to strength. I feel more like myself again.”
According to team principal Laurent Mekies. He drove very well, especially in the second half of the race, but that is not what I saw for the other half of the race...
0.196sec the winning margin... another two or three hundred metres and it might have been gone.
Russell’s third victory of the season and a deserved one. Had to win it twice almost.
“That was a fast last stint... after that double yellow I lost the boost, had no power, thought he was going to get us,” Russell says on the radio.
🟨Bottas has gone into the barriers at turn 15 which helps Russell... or should do...
But Verstappen is now closer than ever coming out of that corner... but I think he has it...
A bit. Some leaf debris on the track on the run down to turn three, quite a chunky branch. Russell cannot afford a mistake here...
The gap is 1.4sec as they cross the line to start the final lap...
Tenth for the Williams man. Hulkenberg is the man who is demoted.
I think Russell has this under control. Antonelli, in fifth, within two seconds of Leclerc.
As it stands Russell would take out 15 points from Antonelli’s title lead.
Lindblad up into eighth with a fine move on Oliver Bearman at turn three.
Nothing to be worried about, he is told. He just brushed the wall at turn 15. Not very heavily. Oh, it was at 16, and that was a bit harder.
Antonelli has some floor damage and isn’t making a great deal of time up on Leclerc.
Closer than ever to leader Russell.
A good day for Haas in the offing, 10 points on their way as it stands.
No further action for Lawson and Lindblad... but Max Verstappen has been noted for failing to follow the race directors’ instructions. Not sure what that is about.
Next up is Charles Leclerc. A podium might be a bit too much here but fourth is certainly on the cards in a weekend of damage limitation.
They are fighting for fifth place. Verstappen is able to stay within a second of Russell which gives him the extra boost but does not seem to be close enough to try a move.
The Lindblad and Lawson incident has been noted, though no word yet on the Colapinto incident. I mean, he’s out of the race but should be given a grid penalty for that...
He locks up at turn one and goes straight on dropping waaaaay back down to 15th. More points for Antonelli. Piastri was defending from Hadjar there but that has ruined what was a strong weekend for him.
Russell has edged more than a second ahead of Verstappen.
Russell goes a bit earlier this time and manages his lead very well. Still work to do, though, if Verstappen can cling on. Can Antonelli scythe through the field from here? He was 30-odd seconds behind Russell before the first SC period.

A divebomb from the Alpine driver at turn one and he barrels into Gasly, who then in turn hits Norris. Madness. Lindblad also locks up and went into the side of his team-mate, Liam Lawson, who spins around.
“Man, I love being taken out by my team-mate. That’s very sick,” he says.

Not sure how many drivers out of the race... but Lando Norris is one of them.
Will this be another Safety Car? Surely. Yes. Eventually. Norris out of the race and masses of debris at turn one.
Right, let’s hope for some action.
The bigger and bad news is that his hard-earned lead has been wiped out. The good news is that he is on soft tyres and Piastri behind him is on mediums.
I don’t think there will be a reshuffling of the order here. Surprised we haven’t had a red flag because Albon’s car is so far into the wall and is not easy to remove.

Antonelli comes into the pits as do a few others. The leaders not able to make the most of this instantly, but this could be a relatively lengthy stoppage so I imagine Russell will also be able to stop under the SC, or change his tyres under the red flag, if that is called.
He locks up at turn one and goes straight on to the massive run-off area... loses a place to Gasly and one to Antonelli, who is up into eighth now.

Hundreds of thousands of people have greeted Pope Leo XIV in the centre of Paris for a giant open-air Mass.
Crowds cheered as the pontiff moved down the Champs-ÃlysÃ©es Avenue beneath the Arc de Triomphe, waving to crowds from his popemobile.
The head of the Catholic Church blessed several babies as he stopped at different stages along the avenue as chants of "Leo, Leo" rang out.
More than half a million people are expected to attend the event in the heart of the French capital on Saturday and a special altar has been built on the Place de la Concorde for the ceremony.
French President Emmanuel Macron, who met Leo for an hour of talks on Friday, will not be at any of the Pope's Masses during his four-day visit to France, largely to avoid breaching France's strict separation of state and religion.
But the Champs-ÃlysÃ©es Mass will be attended by Macron's wife Brigitte and Prime Minister SÃ©bastien Lecornu.
Several candidates for next year's presidential election are also expected to attend.
Marine Le Pen of the hard-right National Rally party and conservative Bruno Retailleau were both pictured at the Place de la Concorde ahead of the event, while centrists Edouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal are also due to be there.
Mayor of Le Havre and former French Prime Minister Edouard Philippe and former Prime Minister Francois Fillon were both also seen at the Place de la Concorde.
Thousands have gathered along Champs-Elysees Avenue ahead of Pope Leo's open-air Mass
Earlier on Saturday, the Pope met migrants as he visited the Maison Bakhita centre, an association supporting refugees, and praised the organisation for inviting "us to see those who are invisible".
During the visit Leo said it was "possible to encounter one another and to live together in dignity and peace".
He also stressed the "the fundamental role of women in building a civilisation of love".
The Pope also issued a warning about the dangers of artificial intelligence (AI) at the start of his visit to France on Friday.
Leo cautioned against "losing our humanity amid a paradise of machines" in wide-ranging remarks to Church and state officials at the ÃlysÃ©e Palace.
Why is the Pope in France?
Large crowds are expected throughout the pontiff's trip, which the Church believes reflects a growing spirituality among the French and other Europeans.
On Sunday, 150,000 have signed up to attend mass in the Pyrenean sanctuary of Lourdes.
The Pope will be in Metz, in northeast France, on Monday where he will pay tribute to Robert Schuman (1886-1963), a founding father of the European Union and a fervent Catholic who is today a candidate for beatification.
Born in Chicago in 1955, Pope Leo XIV was originally called Robert Prevost â a French name.
His paternal grandmother was born in Le Havre in Normandy in 1894. When she married in the US many years later, she and her Italian husband took the name Prevost, which had been her mother's maiden name.

articles.title_orig: Trump rejects Iran's conditional ceasefire proposal, WSJ reports, as Saudi coalition intercepts projectiles
articles.title_zh: Trump rejects Iran's conditional ceasefire proposal, WSJ reports, as Saudi coalition intercepts projectiles
articles.content_orig:
United States President Donald Trump has reportedly ruled out an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week, according to unnamed US officials cited by The Wall Street Journal.
Trump’s rejection comes just hours after Iran put forward a new roadmap to opening the strait, through which one-fifth of global oil and natural gas is shipped during peacetime – and days after the US president threatened to “annihilate” Iran from the floor of the UN General Assembly.
Here’s what we know about Trump’s response to the proposal and what could come next in the conflict.
The proposal lays out a roadmap to open the Strait of Hormuz with normal maritime passage within a week.
Speaking to reporters on Friday, Iran’s Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi, said the proposal calls for the US to take actions it committed to under the failed June 17 Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on an accelerated timeframe.
Those actions include releasing $12bn in frozen Iranian assets, lifting Iranian oil sanctions and ending the US’s naval blockade on Iranian ports, Araghchi told reporters at a private media briefing on Thursday, according to The New York Times. He also said all hostilities, including in Lebanon, where Israel still occupies part of the south of the country, must cease during the seven-day period.
Araghchi said once the US conditions are met – which he estimated would take four or five days – the Strait of Hormuz could be reopened and negotiations with the US on a “final deal” would start on day seven.
He said the process could begin as soon as the US accepts the plan.
“The choice now rests with the United States,” said Araghchi. “Iran does not accept coercion, threats or intimidation.”
The US government has not publicly responded to the plan.
However, The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump had quickly ruled it out, citing unnamed US officials.
They said Trump was sceptical about whether Iran would fulfil US demands. Trump’s most persistent demands have been that Iran never be able to acquire a nuclear weapon and that it restore free passage in Hormuz.
Iran says it will not discuss its nuclear programme until the conditions it has laid down are met, which has led to an impasse between the two sides.
Meanwhile, a US official has told Al Jazeera that Washington is in no hurry to respond to Iran’s proposal and that it sees itself as being in a strong position with respect to the Strait of Hormuz.
Late on Friday night, Trump posted an image of a map on his Truth Social platform that labelled it “Trump Strait”.
Trump has previously said the US has “total control” over the waterway and threatened to designate it as a US territory . Iran strongly denied that, saying it has complete control of the strait.
Yes, but mostly indirectly. At the UN General Assembly in New York this week, Qatar has been passing messages between the two sides as an intermediary.
Both the US and Iran have said the door to diplomacy remains open and a US official told Al Jazeera that ongoing mediated talks are “positive and constructive”.
Qatar, a key mediator in the conflict, said its foreign minister spoke with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Friday about de-escalation and the conditions for renewed dialogue.
Earlier this week, US officials, including special envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, held mediated discussions with Iranian counterparts in New York, a meeting Trump described as “very good”.
Nevertheless, there is “an enormous amount of scepticism in Washington that the two countries are on the same page,” according to Thomas Warrick, senior fellow at the Atlantic Council.
“I think that the best we can hope for is that this offer from the Iranian foreign minister does lead to further discussions to try to clarify what preconditions Washington is willing to work with,” Warrick told Al Jazeera.
Possibly towards renewed hostilities.
According to the US officials cited in The Wall Street Journal, Trump told his aides he expects to carry out a new bombing campaign against Iran after the US midterm elections in November.
That comes after Trump told the UN General Assembly he was considering whether to “annihilate” Iran and “drive them into hell” in the absence of a deal.
At the same time, Trump has said he believes a deal to end the conflict will come shortly after the midterms.
Paul Musgrave, an associate professor of government at Georgetown University in Qatar, told Al Jazeera that Trump “doesn’t want to end the war on unfavourable terms” and that the result of November’s elections will likely help steer his policy.
If Trump’s Republican party suffers severe setbacks in the elections – and loses its majority in Congress – he may opt for “unilateral actions, including perhaps a resumption of warfare”, said Musgrave.
“That would also mean that Iran would have delivered a really stinging political blow to President Trump,” Musgrave continued, adding this could trigger short-term escalation, “followed by negotiation so that the White House doesn’t look like it’s just surrendering”.

articles.title_orig: Roads flood in New Jersey, inundate some homes, as major signs of nor’easter take shape
articles.title_zh: Roads flood in New Jersey, inundate some homes, as major signs of nor’easter take shape
articles.content_orig:
Surf breaks along the rocky coastline, with the twin lighthouses of Thatcher Island visible in the distance, during the early stages of a nor'easter Friday, Sept. 25, 2026, in Gloucester, Mass. Robert F. Bukaty/FR172387 AP Photo hide caption
Thousands were without power on the U.S. East Coast on Friday night as roads flooded in some coastal New Jersey communities, the first major signs of a powerful nor'easter expected to create dangerous conditions through the weekend.
Tens of millions of people are in the path of the storm already beginning to lash the region with strong winds and rain as it braces for much more. Dangerous flooding is expected along the Mid-Atlantic coast, particularly near New Jersey and Delaware, according to the National Weather Service.
In the coastal New Jersey borough of Surf City, water, with waves rippling along its surface, flooded the streets, inundating some homes. About 34 miles (54.7 kilometers) up the coast in the borough of Manasquan, where some roads were also flooding, Mayor Mike Mangan said he expected "a lot of water in the streets for a long time." A voluntary evacuation had been issued earlier in some low-lying areas of the community.
Concerts were canceled, along with dozens of flights going into airports in Boston, Nantucket and Martha's Vineyard on Friday and Saturday. Several airlines were offering to waive some change or cancellation fees for some East Coast flights through the weekend.
Brian Kelly, the mayor of the tiny New Jersey beach community Sea Bright, said the borough is bracing for winds up to 50 mph (80 kph) and flooding that could reach up to 6 feet (1.8 meters) on some streets. Officials expect the flooding to start Saturday and worsen by midday.
"It's going to be worse than average. We do have probably one or two flooding events a year, sometimes more, sometimes less, but I think this one will be closer to an Irene-scale flooding event," Kelly said, referencing the 2011 storm that caused major flooding in the Northeast. "I hope I'm wrong, but that's my gut feeling."
Kelly hopes hundreds of residents living in low-lying areas will consider evacuating. He said the town will open its recreation center for evacuees.
Peak wind gusts could approach 60 to 65 mph (97 to 105 kph) on Cape Cod, Martha's Vineyard and Nantucket on Friday night and Saturday, compared with about 50 to 55 mph (80 to 89 kph) around Boston and 35 to 40 mph (56 to 64 kph) farther inland, according to Matthew Belk, a meteorologist with NWS in Norton, Massachusetts.
"It's definitely going to be a case of the closer to the coast you are, the more impacts from the storm you're likely to see," Belk said.
Belk said nor'easters are not unusual as New England moves into fall, but one concern this early in the season is that leaves remain on the trees, creating more wind resistance. That could increase the risk of downed limbs, which in turn can cause power outages and leave debris in roads, he said.
Along the Atlantic coasts of New Jersey and Delaware, wind gusts could reach 60 mph (96.6 kph), according to NWS. In southeastern Connecticut and eastern Long Island, New York, gusts could get almost as high, potentially downing tree limbs and power lines.
More than 200 flights to and from airports in Boston, Nantucket, Martha's Vineyard and New York had been canceled Friday, and more cancellations were already in place for Saturday.
Meanwhile, the Red Sox announced their weekend series against the Chicago Cubs would be adjusted. The team moved the Sunday afternoon game to Friday to create a split doubleheader. Separately, Ed Sheeran announced that his high-profile Friday and Saturday shows at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, would be canceled due to the storm.
The public ferry service connecting Cape Cod with the islands of Nantucket and Martha's Vineyard was experiencing widespread cancellations Friday due to strong winds and choppy water.
In Rhode Island, ferries were also canceled for Block Island. The disrupted ferry service was expected to also spill into Saturday.
For people who regularly travel to and from the islands, the possibility of getting stuck on one side or the other is "part of life," said Sean Driscoll, a spokesperson for the Woods Hole, Martha's Vineyard and Nantucket Steamship Authority. Most people have backup plans in place for when boats are canceled.
"It's a nuisance, but you know, we know what to do with this kind of stuff at this point," he said. "This is not out of the realm of ordinary."
Ashley Destino of Gloucester, a coastal city in northern Massachusetts, enjoyed a stroll along the beach with her two young children before preparing to hunker down at home during the storm.
"We came to the beach on Friday afternoon because we knew we were going to be inside all weekend," said Destino, who has Legos and arts and crafts activities prepared to entertain her two children, ages 7 and 4.
She also prepared by securing her boat with additional lines, and her husband pulled out a generator in case the electricity goes out.

articles.title_orig: At Least 4 Dead After Explosion in Athens Tourist District
articles.title_zh: At Least 4 Dead After Explosion in Athens Tourist District
articles.content_orig:
The building in the Plaka district was reduced to rubble strewn with household items
Six people have died, including a British national, in an explosion that destroyed a building housing a holiday rental property in the historic centre of Athens.
The blast on Friday happened in the Plaka area of the Greek capital, a neighbourhood close to tourist sites such as the Acropolis.
Four American holidaymakers were among the dead, along with a UK national and Greek national - reportedly an elderly couple who lived in the same building.
Pictures from the scene on Saturday showed emergency service workers searching through rubble, with a gas leak the suspected cause of the blast.
All six bodies had been recovered by Saturday afternoon. Athens Mayor Haris Doukas said: "We are talking about an incredible disaster."
The tourists were confirmed to be missing when they did not arrive for their flight at Athens airport later on Friday, Reuters news agency reported citing local police.
The three-storey building completely collapsed due to the force of the blast, with neighbouring buildings damaged and debris scattered across the road.
Investigators at the scene believe the blast was caused by a gas leak
Local media reported people were injured by material scattered across nearby streets and some buildings needed to be evacuated.
Excavators and thermal imaging cameras have been used at the scene to search for survivors.
The explosion happened on a small road situated between two of Athens' most visited sites - the Acropolis and the Temple of Olympian Zeus.
A UK Foreign Office spokesperson said: "We are aware of a suspected explosion in Athens and are in touch with the local authorities."

articles.title_zh: She grew up under Soviet rule. Now EU's top diplomat warns Europe against giving Russia what it wants
articles.content_orig:
Deputy Editor, National Security and Foreign Policy
The head of Europe's oldest and largest intergovernmental organization told Newsweek that the continent may not be adequately prepared for the kind of modern, hybrid warfare associated with a potential clash with Russia amid rising tensions.
In an interview on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, Council of Europe Secretary-General Alain Berset said that European countries must "evolve to confront, to face, the challenge of hybrid threats."
At this time, he said, "we are not really well-prepared for this, to be honest."
Berset, a two-time former Swiss president who has served as chief of the 46-member Council of Europe since September 2024, pointed to transformations in the Russia-Ukraine war as an example of how war has changed so drastically in recent years, with tanks and other methods of conventional warfare swapped out for drones capable of carrying out death and destruction at further range, lower cost and far less direct accountability.
And the hybrid threat landscape is not limited to the battlefield at a time when not only drones, but also online interference campaigns, have increasingly penetrated across Europe, exploiting a wave of political upheaval that risks upending the liberal consensus.
"It is evolving quite rapidly, and we need to adapt to this," Berset said. "But I think the main point about hybrid threats is not only the drones and the threats while flying over country and so on. The most important thing in this context I think it is about information and about infrastructure and information manipulation and information interference."
On this front, he acknowledged "some weaknesses, probably in the energy systems, in the security system, in infrastructure in general." And here, too, he felt Europe was still in the process of catching up.
"And I think maybe we are not well-prepared for this," Berset said. "But it is an evolution."
While recognizing the scale of the present challenge, Berset pointed to some clear indications that Europe was on the right track.
"On the very short term, I think we are maybe seeing that there is a gap between what is needed and what we have," Berset said. "But at the same time, if we consider the recent evolutions, let's just say the last two or three years, I mean the institutional evolution is huge.
"The decisions, for example, to become much more independent and strong in armament and defense has been taken and it is evolving and it's a good thing."
Defense spending among the 27 European Union member states—all of which are also in the Council of Europe—is projected to exceed $516 billion this year, a 75 percent increase from just five years ago. The EU's ReArm Europe Plan/Readiness 2030 campaign also aims to pledge up to $800 billion in additional defense spending.
But there is another budget need Berset identifies to secure the values of human rights, democracy and rule of law for which the Council of Europe has striven since its founding in 1949.
"We need the same resolve through the investment for democratic security and democratic values and strong institutions," Berset said.
The task is particularly urgent, Berset argued, as while "we are seeing right now strong investments in armies, different armaments" across Europe, "at the same time we are witnessing a strong backsliding in democratic values and the quality of debates everywhere."
The risk of this trajectory, he warned, could create a situation in the coming years in which "over-armed countries" have "no democratic control" to restrain them, thus satisfying security needs but lacking the kind of institutions that uphold the Council of Europe's long-standing mission.
The solution he provides is to enhance investment in the combined concept of "democratic security."
"It means to have a comprehensive approach where we have democratic institutions in a country able to control what's happening and not having an extremist group winning elections somewhere because of manipulations, or a lot of other reasons, and then taking control of super well-armed armies," Berset said.
Yet, already, political forces seeking to undermine the status quo have gained considerable ground across Europe.
The most notable example of late is the historic showing by the far-right Alternative for Deutschland (AfD) party in northeastern Germany in this month's state elections, bringing the group to the precipice of obtaining a majority that would empower nationalist forces in the country for the first time since World War II.
The phenomenon is far from isolated. Right-wing movements with varying ideological standings but often united through nationalistic and populist tendencies have secured major momentum in other European nations as well, including Austria, France and the Netherlands.
Berset recalls that "this is not the first time that something like this is happening" in Europe, looking back to previous manifestations of disruptive political movements over the past century. In fact, he said such processes were part of the "living body" that constitutes European democracy.
He argued that the strength of that democracy was rooted in its capacity to "absorb shocks," of which the continent—like much of the world—has undergone many in recent years.
"We have huge sequence of crisis, since the financial crisis, rise of inequalities, debt crisis, difficulties for the states to deliver for the citizens, the war in Ukraine and what it meant for Europe in 2014 to have the invasion of Crimea," Berset said. "Then we have the rise of so-called populist parties, then we had the COVID crisis."
Add to that the "acceleration also with social media, communication, AI and with all the consequences and the information," including deepfakes and experts forecasting a 10 percent to 20 percent chance of human extinction, and Berset said it was only natural that citizens may become disillusioned.
"It is for the people, for the citizens, really complicated right now to understand what does this mean exactly and where is the world going," Berset said. "What does it mean for myself from my perspective, for my children?
"When I was young, it was bright. It was quite clear. It was like a highway. Now, it's impossible to predict what will happen in three or five years."
But Berset emphasized that the strategy being pursued by the Council of Europe was "not trying to fix the past," but rather meet modern challenges with a new set of tools that could reinvigorate and reinforce democratic principles without compromising on free-speech tenets.
"It is a balance not easy to find," Berset said. "Because the first reaction when we are not well prepared is to police speech, is to ban parties, is arrest people, and everything is OK, but you are creating the next wave of problems with this."
One factor that separates the current crisis from Europe's previous bouts with internal and external threats since World War II is a shift in the position of the United States.
While President Donald Trump has pushed in favor of European rearmament, he has done so as part of a campaign to shift the burden of security to allies while simultaneously launching frequent salvos of criticism toward the kind of liberal politics he associates with his Democratic rivals at home.
At times, this has manifested in direct endorsements of nationalist movements, such as the AfD, whose first-place results he hailed as a popular reaction to "horrible immigration rules and regulations."
In other instances, Trump has openly questioned U.S. security commitments in Europe, threatening to withdraw from NATO and downplaying fears of a looming Russian escalation despite a growing chorus of warnings being issued by European leaders.

CNN, MS NOW, and Politico reporters were allowed back into the White House Thursday after a federal judge ordered President Donald Trump to immediately restore their press access.
The re-entry came after a chaotic morning, during which the three outlets filed an emergency request for a hearing, accusing the Trump Administration of having “repeatedly violated” the court order and refusing several reporters access to the White House grounds. "This morning, journalists from each of CNN, MS NOW, and Politico attempted to enter the White House and were turned away, and Secret Service agents confiscated the hard pass of journalists whose hard passes had not previously been confiscated," the outlets said in the court document.
Judge Timothy Kelly had given the Trump Administration until 12:30 p.m. ET to respond to the outlets' filing.
In a court filing of its own, the White House said it "began the process" of reinstating press badges shortly at 7:25 a.m. ET and laid out a timeline of what followed. TIME has reached out to the White House for comment.
Early Thursday, in a District of Columbia court, Judge Kelly issued a temporary restraining order of 14 days against the ban, saying it “likely violated” the media outlets’ “constitutional due process rights.” He ordered that journalists from the banned media outlets should have their White House access reinstated “until further order of the court or the expiration of this temporary restraining order.”
In a statement to TIME, Ted Boutrous, the lawyer representing the news outlets, said “this is a strong ruling vindicating freedom of the press, due process and the rule of law. We greatly appreciate the court’s swift action.”
The order came in response to a lawsuit filed against the Trump Administration by CNN, MS NOW, and Politico on Monday, in which the outlets argued the ban was a “direct assault” on the First Amendment and violated their Fifth Amendment due process rights.
Outlining his ruling, Kelly said the outlets had “shown a likelihood of success, at least on their Fifth Amendment procedural due process claim.” The Fifth Amendment protects Americans from being “deprived of life, liberty, or property, without due process of law.” Kelly determined that the outlets were “likely to succeed in showing that their hard passes were revoked without constitutionally adequate due process.”
The judge also rejected the Trump Administration's assertion that the media ​ban was motivated by “national security” concerns. “Certainly, that is not what President Trump said when he announced that he was ‘banning’ plaintiffs from the WhiteHouse—instead, he focused on the alleged lack of truthfulness and negativity of plaintiffs’ reporting,” Kelly wrote, referencing Trump’s “fake news” reasoning .
The Justice Department, in a legal filing on Tuesday, said the outlets had “received adequate notice” of the ban (a point contested by Kelly) and insisted “the President’s actions are lawful under the First Amendment.”
Ahead of Thursday’s order, Trump dismissed the legal challenge over the ban and indicated he regretted appointing Judge Kelly in 2017.
Vowing to fight any legal block on his ban, Trump insisted : “Almost without question and, as usual, we’ll go for appeal, because fake news people and publications that only write negatively, and who violate our national security by writing false and defamatory stories with unknown ‘sources,’ shouldn’t be allowed access to the [Oval Office].”
However, in the court filing, Kelly stated that “temporary restraining orders are generally unappealable.”
Instead, during the 14-day period, the court “will set a schedule for expedited briefing on a motion for a preliminary injunction,” allowing Trump and the media outlets to submit further evidence for Kelly to consider.
“Either the preliminary injunction will be issued or denied,” says Eugene Volokh, a law professor at UCLA who specializes in the First Amendment. “The temporary restraining order would then lapse, and whichever side loses can then appeal to the D.C. Circuit.”
Instead of an appeal, Trump could file for emergency relief from the D.C. court, similar to how CNN, MS NOW, and Politico did Thursday, according to experts.
But “emergency relief is usually harder to get than a resolution through appeal,” says Volokh.
Trump has a turbulent history with the media. In 2018, he revoked the White House press credentials of Jim Acosta, who was then a CNN correspondent, after a tense exchange during a news conference.
CNN challenged the decision in court and it was Judge Kelly who ordered the White House to reinstate the reporter’s press pass.
Volokh says that legal precedent in the D.C. Circuit, used in both the ongoing case and that of Acosta, has “already been set” for areas of the White House usually open to the media, including the press briefing room.
“The government can't exclude reporters based on viewpoint, and cannot take away a press pass without due process, without some sort of hearing opportunity to be heard, an explanation of what it is that they supposedly did wrong, what rules they violated,” he says.
In light of this, an appeal from the Trump Administration after a preliminary injunction would likely be rejected in the D.C. Circuit, he argues. However, the President may find a better chance in the Supreme Court.
“Generally speaking, the First Amendment does not secure a right of access to government office buildings,” says Volokh, once again noting the exception of areas usually granted access for press. "The same position could be taken by the Supreme Court, and [it] might say: 'Look, the government can pick and choose whom to allow on its property,'" he says.
There has been an outpouring of solidarity among other media outlets in light of the ban.
CNN, one of five U.S. news outlets in the White House press pool that rotates responsibility for pooled live video coverage, was scheduled to cover Trump's trip to the U.N. General Assembly in New York on Monday. When they were restricted from doing so, other major television networks declined to replace CNN’s pool crew.
In a rare joint statement, ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News, and NBC said : “The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No Administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.”
In a further show of support, some media publications—including the New York Times and Washington Post —announced they would hold off on publishing or distributing still photographs taken as part of the White House pool coverage.
On Wednesday, 49 media organizations filed a legal brief voicing their support of CNN, MS NOW, and Politico. “Stripping journalists and news outlets of their rights because of perceived editorial viewpoint violates decades of Supreme Court jurisprudence and is impermissible in any type of forum, including the White House,” the brief argued.

articles.title_orig: ‘To Catch a Predator’ Host Chris Hansen Watches Robert Pattinson’s ‘Primetime’ — and He’s Not a Fan
articles.title_zh: ‘To Catch a Predator’ Host Chris Hansen Watches Robert Pattinson’s ‘Primetime’ — and He’s Not a Fan
articles.content_orig:
Former To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen was interviewed on his podcast Friday to give his unfiltered reaction to A24 ‘s unauthorized, dramatized film about parts of his life, Primetime , which he called overly dramatic, detached from reality, and a “fever dream” — while giving Robert Pattinson ‘s performance a “D” grade.
Primetime , which opens Friday in the U.S., is set in 2006 and follows Pattinson’s fictionalized version of Hansen as the popular To Catch a Predator segment on NBC’s Dateline grows into its own primetime block on the network. On the show, Hansen blurred journalistic lines by working with law enforcement and the watchdog group Perverted Justice to intercept adult men as they arrived, unbeknownst to them, at a sting house to meet a minor they’d met online for sex. The men were typically arrested as a result. The series drew mixed reactions, with concerns about potential entrapment-law violations at the forefront of the criticism.
In a brief segment produced for his video podcast, Have a Seat with Chris Hansen , the former NBC News journalist is seen exiting a Times Square AMC after viewing the film for the first time at a Thursday night screening — his first look at the indie drama since its theatrical release. He’s then asked for his first reaction to the Lance Oppenheim-directed film .
“It’s hard for me to — obviously, I’m not a judge, because the character is based on me,” he said. “I think because the character is so detached from reality, from anything I’ve ever experienced then or now doing the investigations — I’m not sure what the point of it was.”
The rest of the podcast episode has Hansen discussing the film, its director and Pattinson’s portrayal of him with Fox News’ Jesse Watters. Hansen railed against the movie throughout.
Oppenheim has said he conceived Primetime after receiving a personalized Cameo video from the To Catch a Predator host. Hansen said on his podcast that he spoke to a mutual friend before seeing the film, and that Oppenheim told the friend it was “something to the effect of, ‘a love letter to Chris Hansen, and it gets a little weird in the storytelling.'”
Hansen also flagged inaccuracies in the fictionalized version of his life — including scenes involving Jeff Zucker and Stone Phillips that he insists never happened — and said absolutely nothing in the film was close to reality. He assured viewers he’s not the ratings-obsessed figure the script conjures. His biggest gripe, he said, is that the film portrays him as an aloof parent, which he says is far from how he relates to his kids. As for Pattinson’s take on Hansen circa 2006, Hansen had few kind words.
“He’s got work to do. I’m kind of the only guy that counts for this, right?” he said.
Days before seeing the movie, Hansen spoke with The Hollywood Reporter ‘s Seth Abramovich about what he knew of the film. A24 hadn’t reached out to him or the production to explain the premise or ask for his input, he said.
“Based upon what I’ve seen in the trailer and my understanding of what’s been written about the film, they wanted to create something much darker and way more dramatic,” he said. “I think it’s an insult to the thousands of men and women who work hard every day to protect children from predators. They’ve turned something that is very positive, very challenging and not without risk into what is essentially a horror film.”
On Friday, after viewing Primetime , he doubled down with a direct swipe at Oppenheim.
“You have to question the motives of not coming forward and talking to me or anybody I’ve worked closely with over the years,” he said. “They didn’t want to hear that Chris Hansen is a good guy. They didn’t want to hear that this work is important. This director had a dark image of what he wanted to do. He wanted to create a horror-like film with interesting photography, and didn’t want to hear anything else.”
Hansen continues identifying and capturing potential child predators on Takedown with Chris Hansen . Earlier on Friday, Hansen’s TruBlu streaming network dropped the trailer for I’m Chris Hansen , a documentary centered around the host.

articles.title_orig: All the Major Social Media Networks Are Reportedly Refusing Ads for ‘Musk’
articles.title_zh: All the Major Social Media Networks Are Reportedly Refusing Ads for ‘Musk’
articles.content_orig:
Senior Editor, Technology and Politics
So much for free speech. The studio releasing Alex Gibney ’s new Elon Musk documentary Musk is finding itself unable to buy an ad on the biggest social platforms. YouTube , TikTok , and Instagram and Facebook owner Meta are all declining to run the trailer for Musk , along with X itself, The Hollywood Reporter has learned. That last one is perhaps understandable, given its owner. But the rejection by the other platforms has taken distributor Bleecker Street by surprise, and it is internally scrambling to understand why the ad has been rejected, according to a person familiar with the company’s processes who is not authorized to talk about them publicly. The unwillingness of platforms to accept even paid advertising is sure to raise concerns about free speech and the dwindling number of companies that control many of the platforms in this country — and ironically provide a proof-text for the very point the film is coming to make. Gibney’s doc is a four-hour look at a title character who attempts to control the conversation in various ways , including with alleged suppressions on X, which he bought in 2022.
Bleecker Street opens Musk in theaters on Oct. 9. YouTube, TikTok and Meta have all supplied a reason related to “political content” to Bleecker Street reps. The latter two companies’ platforms, by policy, do not allow campaign or other political ads, in Meta’s case largely owing to fallout from the Cambridge Analytica Facebook scandal during the 2016 election. But the Musk trailer, which dropped Thursday, does not appear to fall in the category of the campaign advertising those bylaws were enacted to prevent. It simply contains a shot of a political rally in 2024 and a reference at the end to the 2024 election — the kind of flicks that occur in numerous documentaries and are hardly meant to stump for a particular candidate in an upcoming race.
The reason for YouTube’s rejection is even less clear, as the platform does allow campaign ads, albeit with “paid for” disclosures from vetted candidates.
Bleecker Street has entered an appeal with all three companies. Meta has already rejected the appeal. TikTok and YouTube are still entertaining the petitions. For its part, X has refused to engage with Bleecker Street on the film or even accept advertising for any of its other films on its upcoming calendar. Press reps at Meta, TikTok, YouTube and X did not immediately provide a comment. A Bleecker Street representative confirmed that the ads were initially rejected but said they are continuing to appeal with all three companies besides X in the hope minds can be changed.
Traction on social media is key for a documentary release, which relies on word-of-mouth in a way a big-budget feature doesn’t.
The news also hits a nerve after Universal, which is releasing the film overseas, considered backing away from distributing Musk before capitulating to public pressure and commenting that it is standing by the film (though no details have yet been given).
It is unclear if there has been any communication between ad reps at X and the other social giants. Some other tech firms will also see their leaders under the Hollywood spotlight this fall, with Sony releasing Aaron Sorkin’s Mark Zuckerberg drama The Social Reckoning next month. That film’s trailer is currently available on YouTube.

articles.title_orig: Rogue OpenAI agents accessed US government websites
articles.title_zh: Rogue OpenAI agents accessed US government websites
articles.content_orig:
OpenAI said Friday that its AI agents had gained access to private images belong to ChatGPT users and posted them online, the latest in a string of alarming incidents in which technology developed inside leading AI labs has gone rogue and acted in unintended ways.
The private ChatGPT users’ images, which OpenAI stored on its servers in anonymized form in order to train its AI models, were posted to image hosting websites, the company said in a post on X . A total of 53 images were posted.
The incident, which was first reported by Reuters , was among several new revelations of rogue AI activity at OpenAI that emerged on Friday. The New York Times published new details about the July hack of the Hugging Face website , reporting that the AI agents had created special, shortened web links to evade detection.
And earlier on Friday, OpenAI disclosed that that it has notified dozens of third parties about incidents in which its models either bypassed security controls or used websites in unintended ways. The incidents were discovered by OpenAI amid an internal review triggered by the Hugging Face hack.
“We have not been as fast as we would have liked but we are trying to balance our desire for transparency with gaining a clear understanding from petabytes of agent activity logs, and working with impacted organizations,” OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in a post on X Friday alongside the update on third party notifications.
“Hugging Face is still the most severe event we’ve seen,” he added. “We will be as transparent as we can be subject to things like vulnerabilities in other companies that our agents have found, which will be their call to disclose or not.”
Other leading companies developing the most cutting edge “frontier” AI models, like Anthropic and Google, have also disclosed incidents of rogue activity by their models in recent weeks. The revelations have ignited broad concerns about the speed at which artificial intelligence is evolving, and whether there are sufficient safeguards and regulations in place to ensure that the technology does not completely slip beyond human control. Some AI experts, including researchers within the AI labs, have warned that the technology poses a significant risk of human extinction if proper precautions are not taken.
Altman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, and other tech executives spoke at the UN General Assembly this week, calling for an international framework to manage the development of AI. President Donald Trump however has called the notion that AI poses an existential risk a “hoax.”
The New York Times report, based on research by startup company Parse, described how OpenAI’s agents had created nearly 1 million shortened internet links in July. According to the report, the links contained encoded bits of information that when combined together could function as a computer program. These programs were intended to help the agents bypass defenses like Captcha quizzes, which are designed to block access by bots.
It’s not clear if the leaked images reported by Reuters were part of the Hugging Face incident, or completely separate. OpenAI’s agents apparently got hold of the user images by accessing the company’s own training data. OpenAI did not provide details on whether the images were photos of real people or AI-generated images created by users, and the company did not say exactly where the images had been posted. But OpenAI said the images were posted to image-hosting sites “as links that weren’t publicly listed.”
“We have successfully worked with the hosting providers to remove most of this content and are working to remove the rest,” OpenAI said.

articles.title_orig: Trump cancels nearly $1bn in funding approved by Congress
articles.title_zh: Trump cancels nearly $1bn in funding approved by Congress
articles.content_orig:
President using rare power to revoke expenditure with bipartisan approval to aid immigrant services
Donald Trump is canceling nearly $1bn in spending approved by Congress, the White House announced on Friday, using a rare and contested power to axe funding for immigrant services and diversity-focused initiatives.
Trump’s office of management and budget described the funding cut as focused on “the most harmful government spending”.
Most of the cuts are focused on services for immigrants, including non-profits that serve refugees and unaccompanied minors accused of being in the country illegally. The administration says the funds are no longer necessary because illegal border crossings have diminished considerably.
A White House press release announcing the funding rescissions notes that some of the organizations are led by people who worked in the administration of Democratic president Barack Obama.
Trump’s move was condemned by senator Susan Collins, a Republican in a tough re-election campaign and chair of the Senate appropriations committee.
Collins said in a statement the action came without warning or consultation. She also said she would work to address with colleagues “these illegal actions”.
“Not only is the delay itself an impoundment that was not reported to Congress, but also it is a usurpation of Congress’s appropriations powers,” Collins said. “OMB is an agency of the executive branch. It does not get to decide which programs are worth funding.”
“This is theft from the American people, plain and simple,” Patty Murray, the Washington Democratic senator, who is vice-chair of the appropriations committee said in a statement . “These are funds Congress has delivered on a bipartisan basis and should be helping people – not cut off by a president more focused on building a ballroom than investing in families. Every Republican who voted for these bills should be furious, because [Russell] Vought is saying their votes don’t count.”
Typically, Congress can review the president’s proposed spending cuts before they take effect. But Trump made that all but impossible by announcing them with just five days left in the federal fiscal year. The government accountability office has called the maneuver , known as a “pocket rescission,” illegal.
Collins called it the latest attempt by OMB to “undermine Congress’s constitutional power of the purse”.
A year ago, Trump issued a pocket rescission for the first time in 50 years by blocking $4.9bn in congressionally approved foreign aid. The US supreme court declined to block those rescissions, saying that Trump’s authority over foreign affairs weighed heavily in its decision. This year, Trump is targeting domestic spending.
The use of a pocket rescission fits part of a broader pattern by the Trump administration to exact greater control over the US government, eroding the power of Congress.
The administration has also fired federal workers, imposed a historic increase in tariffs, and started the war in Iran without going through Congress, putting the burden on the judicial branch to determine the limits of presidential power.

articles.title_orig: Taylor Swift unveils never-before-seen Travis Kelce home footage in ‘Cleveland!’ lyric video
articles.title_zh: Taylor Swift unveils never-before-seen Travis Kelce home footage in ‘Cleveland!’ lyric video
articles.content_orig:
Taylor Swift let fans inside her and Travis Kelce’s personal world with the release of a lyric video for “Cleveland!” — one of the new songs off her “The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore” album.
The visuals, released Friday, feature never-before-seen home video footage of Swift and Kelce, both 36, visiting his hometown of Cleveland Heights, Ohio.
Kelce is seen multiple times throughout the video, smiling at the camera as he is driving a car with Swift in the passenger seat.
Swift herself makes an appearance toward the end, with us getting a shot of her in the car Kelce is driving.
Before that, however, someone — seemingly the pop star — is depicted wearing a white dress as the lyrics “Now I’m wearing white” are sung.
However, a source tells Page Six the dress seen in the music video isn’t Swift’s wedding dress she wore to marry Kelce at New York City’s Madison Square Garden in July.
In terms of other Easter eggs, the lyric video features someone — again, presumably Swift herself — wearing roller skates which notably have 13 hearts on them, a nod to the Grammy winner’s favorite number.
“Cleveland!” is Swift’s most Kelce-centric song yet, as it’s a reference to the Kansas City Chiefs tight end’s hometown and features personal lyrics about his childhood home when she sings “that house with the porch is where he lived as a kid.”
“My baby likes what he likes / He already took me to Cleveland / And showed me The Heights!” Swift sings in the track. “So hate all you like / This is the love of my life.”
In another lyric, she sings, “The taste of me is acquired, but it’s his favorite dish.”
That line got a strong reaction from Swifties, with many of them pointing out its double meaning — and calling it the most raunchy lyric since her song “Wood,” off 2025’s “The Life of a Showgirl.”
“Forgive me, it sounds cocky / He (ah!)matized [d–kmatized] me / And opened my eyes / Redwood tree / It ain’t hard to see / His love was the key / That opened my thighs,” Swift sang in “Wood.”
But “Cleveland!” is sentimental, too; Swift also sings, “You only need to find one person in this entire world / Who doesn’t find you completely insufferable / And I have an important announcement to make / I found mine,” in reference to Kelce.
Despite Swift’s “Encore” offering earning mixed reactions from critics and fans, the track “Patient Zero” —one of the four new songs — quickly became Spotify’s most-streamed song by a female artist in a single day in 2026 so far, according to a rep for the music streaming service.
Not only that, but Swift is also the most-streamed female artist in a single day this year, per Spotify.
In addition to “Cleveland!” and “Patient Zero,” Swift also released “Pink Clouding” and “Babylon” Friday.
She’ll debut the star-studded “Patient Zero” music video — starring Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell — Sunday at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards.

articles.title_orig: 2026 WNBA playoffs: Biggest questions for Lynx-Liberty, Aces-Fever and every first-round series
articles.title_zh: 2026 WNBA playoffs: Biggest questions for Lynx-Liberty, Aces-Fever and every first-round series
articles.content_orig:
We've finally made it to Money Time, folks.
The WNBA playoffs will be tipping off this weekend, and we've been blessed with four dynamic matchups with varying degrees of star power, scheme versatility, and all the storylines you can hope for if #narratives are your portion.
For this year's preview, we'll be looking at a big picture question for each series, then sprinkling in some other thoughts and questions that may matter moving forward.
Lynx-Liberty • Dream-Mystics • Valkyries-Wings • Aces-Fever
Lynx (33-11): 3rd in offense, 4th in defense, 2nd in net rating
Liberty (26-18): 6th in offense, 7th in defense, 7th in net rating
Season series: Liberty 2-1
THE BIG QUESTION: Is Olivia Miles ready for playoff pressure?
Don't take this as your typical "rookie experiences her first playoff series" point. I don't doubt, assuming she's healthy enough ( please let the calf be OK), that Miles will be ready from a competitive standpoint.
I mean this more in a literal sense. One of the most fascinating trends in the league to me has been teams progressively picking up Miles higher on the court as the season has gone on. Per Second Spectrum, the pick-up points for Miles have increased every month:
That jump in September is notable, man. Look no further than the most recent matchup between the Lynx and Liberty, where the mixture of Leonie Fiebich , Pauline Astier and Rebekah Gardner took turns hounding Miles well beyond half-court. It's not that Miles is incapable of beating that type of aggression; she certainly has the speed, handle and elite blend of driving juice and playmaking gumption to beat it.
But that kind of ball pressure and length can just … weigh on you. Miles finished that game with 20 points, 8 rebounds and 5 assists – not bad, until you add in that she went 5-of-18 from the field and also turned the ball over five times.
(Also of note: Fiebich on Miles specifically is a cross-match worth monitoring. Assuming Breanna Stewart gets the Napheesa Collier matchup, the Liberty will be empowered to switch any Miles-Collier actions. Having to deal with the collective size of Fiebich and Jonquel Jones , if you want to get Natasha Howard involved as a screener, isn't fun either. During their regular season meetings, the Lynx generated only 0.8 points per possession on trips featuring a Miles-Howard pick-and-roll.)
The broader question of how well the Lynx will deal with physicality certainly looms large, but I think we'll get some early answers based on how successful Miles is dealing with it early in possessions.
You never want to be reductive when it comes to playoff time, but this series may very well be decided by whichever backcourt decides to show up. Beyond Miles, the Lynx will need a quality shotmaking and decision-making series from Courtney Williams . The Liberty are simply a different (and much better) team when Sabrina Ionescu comes to the party, and the mix of drives and defensive ball pressure from Astier will be key in this one.
The Liberty rebounded 31.6% of their own misses this season (5th). The Lynx once again ranked toward the bottom of the league in defensive rebound rate (67.7%, 11th). The paint itself will be an important battleground in this series, but the rebound battle will swing things.
Just to briefly circle back: sign me up for potentially three games of Stewie ( please let the knee be OK) and Phee. We're talking two of the, what, four best players in the league at full-tilt? I'm excited to watch them deal with each other. This is a match made in two-way versatility heaven.
Dream (30-14): 4th in offense, 3rd in defense, 3rd in net rating
Mystics (28-16): 12th in offense, 2nd in defense, 8th in net rating
Season series: Mystics 2-1
THE BIG QUESTION: Whose half-court offense can find daylight?
If you want off-ball hand-fighting, crowded (and dangerous) lanes, and rugged paint play, this is the series for you.
The young Mystics (I refuse) have earned their stripes behind a defense that doesn't let you breathe. Shakira Austin ( please be OK) and Sonia Citron headline this unit; Citron may have been the best wing defender in basketball, while Austin's blend of scheme versatility and rim protection made her a(nother) worthy Defensive Player of the Year candidate. Michaela Onyenwere is a fantastic defender in her own right (with All-Defense level metrics and tracking data to boot), while Kiki Iriafen has quietly grown into a quality defender that can hold her own in space.
On the other side, the Dream boast the likely frontrunner for Defensive Player of the Yea r in Angel Reese , a rangy thief in Rhyne Howard (who would probably be an All-Pro corner in another lifetime), a smaller-but-still-deadly thief in Jordin Canada , plus a pair of defenders in Allisha Gray and Naz Hillmon that can perform at an All-Defense level on any given night.
No team turns you over quite like the Dream; seriously, they forced turnovers on a league-high 19.5% of possessions. That doesn't seem to bode well for a Mystics group that turned the ball over on 19.2% of their possessions, the worst mark in the league.
No team mashes the paint quite like the Mystics, ranking first in the percentage of points that come in the paint, offensive rebound rate, and free throw rate. That doesn't seem to bode well for a Dream group that fouls quiiite a bit (11th in opponent free throw rate).
I've had questions about both of these half-court offenses throughout the year, so it's a bit funny (and fitting) that they have to face each other in the first round.
Tied to the overall paint battle, I wonder what the scoring approach for Howard and Gray will be. Gray's the more consistent downhill threat, and Howard's at her best when she can complement her perimeter shotmaking (44.8% on 9.7 3s against the Mystics this year) with some drives. The Mystics, more than anyone else, have made their lives difficult when they've tried to pressure the rim. Per Second Spectrum, the Mystics had at least one help defender present on 83% of drives from Howard or Gray. Their combined 0.91 PPP clip on drives against the Mystics was their worst against any opponent.
Actually, we'll stay in the paint a beat longer. How impactful will rookie centers Lauren Betts (Mystics) and Madina Okot (Dream) be in this series? With Bri Jones done for the season, Okot will be needed for some important spot minutes. Betts generally keeps the rim protection (and offensive rebounding) train rolling when she checks in for Austin or Iriafen; the Mystics will need that to maintain their paint edge.
Do not sleep on the offensive importance of Canada (she's made a lot of plays in clutch situations) and, on the Mystics' side, Georgia Amoore . Coach of the Year candidate Sydney Johnson has spoken about Amoore's importance as an organizer; if she's able to make enough shots, the Point Sonia lineups could feel like more of a bonus than a necessity.
Valkyries (32-12): 7th in offense, 1st in defense, 1st in net rating
Wings (27-17): 5th in offense, 6th in defense, 6th in net rating
Season series: Valkyries 3-0
THE BIG QUESTION: Can the Wings crack the code on Golden State's defense?
It's not enough to acknowledge the Valkyries having the league's stingiest defense (99.1 defensive rating). Their defense, per PBP Stats, was nearly 10 points better than league average — making it (statistically, at least) the stingiest defense of all time.
The Wings, headlined by the All-Star duo of Paige Bueckers and Jessica Shepard , posted a franchise-best 111.3 offensive rating during the regular season. They could only muster a 97.8 offensive rating across their three winless matchups against the Valkyries this season.
Having the trio of Veronica Burton , Gabby Williams and Kiah Stokes to throw at Bueckers, Arike Ogunbowale (a former All-Star in her own right) and Shepard is quite the luxury, and that's before mentioning the other high-wattage options (former Wings Kaila Charles and Kayla Thornton chief among them) they can and did cycle in.

articles.title_orig: Trump and Chinese president Xi end summit without major agreement on AI
articles.title_zh: Trump and Chinese president Xi end summit without major agreement on AI
articles.content_orig:
Xi’s state visit to the US emphasized personal rapport with the US president, rather than substantial agreements to pause their respective countries’ AI arms race
Donald Trump and Chinese president Xi Jinping wrapped up their Washington summit on Friday, facing criticism that they had squandered an opportunity to pause their countries’ artificial intelligence (AI) arms race.
The three-day state visit emphasised pageantry and personal rapport rather than substantial agreements. The US president and Xi discussed the wars in Iran and Ukraine and the status of Taiwan. Their biggest policy announcement was a modest two-month extension of a trade truce.
But despite the presence of top tech executives at a White House state dinner on Thursday night, Trump and Xi failed to deliver the AI breakthrough that some experts and foreign governments had hoped for amid warnings that the technology could pose an existential threat to humanity.
“It was such a layup,” said Ro Khanna , the top Democrat on the House of Representatives’ select committee on China. “If [Trump] had just said, look, we have established technical working groups and we’ve agreed to a framework that has called for DeepSeek and Moonshot and Alibaba to sit down with Anthropic and OpenAI and Gemini and with technical experts and they’re going to commit to at least a pause on any self-improving AI, he could have looked like he was a statesman taking the lead.
“I believe Xi Jinping would have agreed to some of at least the technical working groups. But he [Trump] didn’t want to; he has no interest in doing that.”
It was the first visit to the White House by a Chinese president in more than a decade and Xi’s second state visit to the US. Three days of pomp and circumstance culminated on Friday with Trump and Xi drinking tea. Trump said ⁠the summit ⁠had produced great strides and that “our ​farmers are going to be happy,” but did not provide details.
The pair then went to the National Archives , where Trump and Xi looked at the original Declaration of Independence, the constitution and Bill of Rights. Trump told reporters they were comparing China’s documents to America’s founding documents. “Ours goes 250 years, which is great, and we’re proud of. Theirs goes 6,000 years. So there’s a little difference between 6,000 and 250. But we’re very proud of our 250.”
On Thursday, Xi acknowledged that the US and China have the “responsibility to develop and manage AI for good” and “ensure that the development of AI is always ​under human control”. China aims to have next-generation smart terminals and AI agents reach more than 90% penetration by 2030.
But Trump – who has repeatedly said the US must forge ahead to maintain its lead over China – appeared more focused on his push to rebrand artificial intelligence as “super intelligence”, later claiming on social media that Xi “seems to like” the term without divulging the substance of their discussions.
Later Trump hosted a black-tie state dinner attended by titans of the tech industry. Bernie Sanders, an independent senator of Vermont, used social media to label a photo of Trump and Xi’s table with guests’ net worth: Elon Musk of SpaceX and Tesla ($928bn), Lisa Su of Advanced Micro Devices ($3.5bn), Jensen Huang of Nvidia ($186bn) and Tim Cook of Apple ($3.1bn). Sanders commented: “A government of, by and for the billionaire class.”
But their counterparts in the Chinese tech industry were not present and there was little sign of either country making even a symbolic gesture to apply the brakes.
Khanna commented: “Trump didn’t have to have some groundbreaking treaty like Reagan and Gorbachev did [on nuclear weapons]. He could have at least said, look, we’re going to have a working group of Chinese and American technologists working together to make recommendations and enforcement and verification of the labs. ”
Jonathan Czin , a fellow in the China Center at the Brookings Institution thinktank in Washington, agrees that an opportunity was missed. “We are in this potentially transformative moment for both countries and for the world and for technology and, instead of having a meeting that would meet the moment, you got theatre of the absurd in lieu of that,” he said.
“Even going into this meeting, you’re dealing with a septuagenarian and octogenarian who may or may not have ever had first-hand contact with actually using AI and what happens with this technology rests on their two shoulders. The only thing they seemed to agree about is that neither of them wants to slow down with this technology, regardless of their actual understanding of it.”
The state visit underlined the contrast between Trump’s treatment of democratic allies such as Canada and authoritarian rivals such as China. He broke from tradition to give Xi a red carpet welcome when he landed at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland.
He also found time to show Xi around the White House, including a gallery wall of presidents where Joe Biden is mockingly depicted as an autopen , a construction site for his White House ballroom and a new helicopter landing pad. “He’s an expert on stone, aside from many other things, and he loves good granite,” Trump said.
But the summit was somewhat overshadowed by Trump’s decision last week to bar CNN, MS Now and Politico from the White House, sparking a legal fight. On Thursday, Chinese state media were welcomed into the White House grounds even as members of America’s free press were frozen out, though later they gained entry. As in May, when Trump visited Beijing , the leaders did not hold a press conference.
Czin of the Brookings Institution added: “I had very low expectations going into this meeting for anything of substance and the meeting managed to underwhelm even those low expectations. We went from the mezzanine down into the basement. In terms of the substance, it’s not clear to me what the US got out of this .”
Senate Democrats also criticised the summit, arguing that Trump failed to secure meaningful concessions from Beijing on trade, security, human rights or AI.
Chuck Schumer, the minority leader in the Senate, said : “As usual, Trump acts based solely on who flatters him at the moment, where the nearest photo op is, and what headline he covets. If you’re a foreign authoritarian, Trump won’t just invite you to visit America, he’ll greet you plane-side.”
Trump and Xi are on track to meet twice more this year. In November, Xi will host the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, and in December the Group of 20 summit will be held at the Trump National Doral Miami golf club in Florida.

articles.title_orig: Supreme Court blocks Trump-backed Missouri congressional map
articles.title_zh: Supreme Court blocks Trump-backed Missouri congressional map
articles.content_orig:
People opposed to a congressional redistricting plan rally outside the Missouri Capitol in Jefferson City, Mo., earlier this month. David A. Lieb/AP hide caption
In a case watched across the country and as voting begins in the midterm elections, the Supreme Court blocked a congressional map in Missouri that was aimed at netting Republicans another seat in the U.S. House.
This is the third time the high court has blocked the redistricting plan that could have helped oust Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver by increasing the number of Republican voters in his district.
The court warned that changing maps now would cause "electoral chaos." The decision requires the state use the same districts provided to voters in 2022 and 2024. That's even though a different map was used in the primaries there last month.
It comes after weeks of conflicting rulings in state courts and federal courts. Elections officials in Missouri already started mailing some absentee ballots last week using the old districts and some argued it would be too late to change them.
Missouri lawmakers passed the new map last year at the behest of President Trump. It was part of his nationwide strategy to draw more GOP-leaning seats to prevent Republicans from losing the House.
Usually, states redistrict at the start of each decade. The redistricting battle set off by Trump ended with the GOP besting the Democrats by tilting about nine or 10 more districts , including Missouri's 5th District , their way. Republicans currently only hold a few seats advantage in the House.
But opponents of the new Missouri map successfully gathered citizen signatures to put it to a vote on the November ballot.
The Missouri Supreme Court ruled earlier this month that the ballot question meant the 2025 GOP-backed map never went into effect and was never law — even though it had been used in the Aug. 4 primaries. The state's high court blamed Republican Secretary of State Denny Hoskins for proceeding with the GOP map in the primaries even though it hadn't been approved by voters.
The U.S. Supreme Court in its ruling Friday backed that up, noting that the state court had said in May — before the primary — that the GOP map would require voter approval before it could be used.
The U.S. Supreme Court had declined on Sept. 10 to intervene in the state court's ruling but allowed the case to continue.
Simultaneously, Republicans sued in federal court and won backing for the GOP map from a federal judge and then, last week, a federal appeals court. That sent the case back to the U.S. Supreme Court, which ruled against Republican lawmakers Friday.
In general, Republicans argued that their map should be used because more than a million Missourians cast votes in the primary using the map. Opponents of redistricting argued voters hadn't approved the map and blamed Republican officials for dragging out the process and of trying to force through the new map.

articles.title_zh: VR Headsets Are So Cooked
articles.content_orig:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg is continuing his metaverse while simultaneously pushing forward on AI agents.
At Meta Connect , the Facebook co-founder revealed on Wednesday the Meta VR Glasses, a smaller and slimmer device compared to the company's older Quest-branded family of VR headsets, and a handheld device called the Muse Charm that works with the company's recently released Muse AI personal agent . He revealed the products while speaking on stage at the annual Connect conference for developers.
Zuckerberg shared few details about what Muse Charm can do, only to say that people will be able to speak to the gadget to interact with their Meta AI agents "without having to unlock a phone or open an app." He didn't say how much it would cost, but said that Meta needs to "finalize laying out the components" and is "planning to have this ready to ship in time for the holidays in December."
"We've packed a lot of technology with this little guy," Zuckerberg said. "So, if you're not wearing glasses, this is going to be by far the fastest way to talk to your Muse and to show it what's going on around you."
The Meta VR Glasses are slimmer and lighter than the company's older Quest-branded VR headsets, but they are also more expensive, costing $1,299 when they go on sale in spring 2027. They represent Meta's first VR device since 2024, when the company debuted the $299 Quest 3S. The Meta VR Glasses are powered by an external puck that houses a Qualcomm processor and battery, allowing it to function as a mini-computer that also helps reduce the glasses' overall weight and size. The glasses are able to display better visuals than the older Quest headset, and contain sensors that track users' eyes and hand movements, which reduces the need to use controllers to interact with the device.
"We have built a new kind of VR device that delivers the same magical feeling of presence and immersion, high-resolution displays and views of the world around you in a form factor that is a pair of glasses for the first time," Zuckerberg said.
